title: Month three, still no label
old_caption: Three months of dates and still no label? Time won't define it for you. A calm, honest conversation will, and you're allowed to start it.

title: Couple on Saturday, strangers by Monday
old_caption: Pancakes and matching scarves on Saturday, "busy week!" on Monday. Notice the pattern, name it kindly, and ask for the weekday version too.

title: Cropped out of the photo
old_caption: Always just an elbow in their photos? You don't need to be posted to feel secure. You need to know where you stand, so ask for a straight answer.

title: Do I get them a holiday gift?
old_caption: Five weeks in and frozen in the gift aisle? Skip the price spiral. Ask what they're doing for the holidays, and a small, thoughtful card is never wrong.

title: Everyone else already calls it a relationship
old_caption: When your friends already ask how your person is, they're seeing something real. If everyone can see it, the two of you can say it out loud.

title: Jealous with no "right" to be
old_caption: Feeling jealous when you're "not official" isn't a crime, it's a clue. Skip the tests. Tell them what you actually want with them.

title: Rehearsing the talk in the mirror
old_caption: Eleven rehearsals, one easel, one pillow scream. The real speech is short: I like you. I'd like more. You? Then listen to what they say.

title: "I'm not looking for anything serious." "Me neither!"
old_caption: Said "me neither" when you meant "me, very much"? Agreeing to less than you want isn't chill, it's hiding. You're allowed to say what you're looking for.

title: Only texts after midnight
old_caption: "hey stranger" at 12:47, silence at noon. Late-night texts can feel close. Notice who makes plans with you before noon.

title: Was that a date?
old_caption: "Wanna grab food?" No decoder ring needed. Just ask, "as a date?" Clarity is cute, and the answer might be the one you're hoping for.
